scope: Implement the accepted light design system and palette, resolve dark/light token conflict, and normalize persisted per-user theme settings to light.

findings.evidence: frontend/src/App.vue and frontend/src/views/ProfileView.vue each load settings and define applyTheme; both can toggle p-dark. frontend/src/main.ts enables darkModeSelector .p-dark. frontend/src/styles/main.css uses semantic surface/text tokens, including distinct page and header surfaces. User screenshots show a dark body with a light header and low-contrast account text.
findings.impact: Theme selection has two frontend owners and allows a partial dark appearance. Shared semantic tokens and one light-mode policy are required to prevent incompatible surface and text colors.
findings.exit_condition: A single light appearance policy is used at bootstrap/profile; no runtime path enables p-dark or follows OS dark preference; reviewed screens use compatible foreground and surface tokens.
findings.next_action: Implement the approved palette through shared tokens, remove duplicate theme application, and audit shared surfaces/components.

findings.evidence: user_settings.theme is stored in PostgreSQL, defaults to system in the model and migration 20261020_0009_user_profiles.py, and the PATCH schema accepts system/light/dark. The user explicitly chose to migrate all saved values to light.
findings.impact: Changing persisted preferences and the API/model default affects durable state and may affect a frontend version that still submits system or dark.
findings.exit_condition: A migration converts all existing settings to light, new rows default to light, transition API behavior is compatible, and migration/restore semantics are tested on disposable databases.
findings.next_action: Implement conversion and API transition with an explicit local snapshot/restore procedure; do not mutate shared or production databases.

findings.evidence: The current worktree is on main at 74901be and has uncommitted changes in frontend/src/App.vue, frontend/src/main.ts, frontend/src/styles/main.css, docs/design-system.md, docs/data-model.md, and DOCS.md; these overlap planned implementation/documentation changes.
findings.impact: Editing these files before the existing changes are checkpointed or isolated could overwrite or mix prior user work with this implementation.
findings.exit_condition: The existing changes affecting planned files are checkpointed/integrated or the implementation starts in a task-owned worktree from that checkpoint.
findings.next_action: Preserve current changes and resolve their checkpoint before starting affected implementation phases.
